name: block_column
title: a stack of game blocks on the 2 x 2 grid, each a cube 5 plates tall, textured by mixing shades.
why: The base unit of any blocky build: a pillar, a tower corner, or a stone or wood block of the right cube size, in mixed shades.
note: The scale rule (2 x 2 studs, 5 plates a block) as a part recipe; the other sketches here share it. Key parts are very common.

name: raised_module_base
title: a slab of game terrain on dirt-colored legs, one brick off the table, like a chunk cut out of a block world.
why: The base for any blocky scene: a slab on dirt legs, cut out of the world, that butts against the next module on the 2-stud grid.
note: Related to landing_zone; here the slab stands on brick legs a brick up, with seams on legs.

name: module_link_block
title: blocks set across the seam of two terrain modules, locking them into one scene and reading as one more grass block.
why: Locking two terrain modules together so the joint reads as one more grass block.
note: The book drops links into notches left in the module tops; this sketch sets them on top of the two modules, which needs no notch but stands a block proud.

name: grass_block
title: single raised blocks scattered over a lawn, each a dirt brick under a grass top with one stud.
why: Scattering raised grass, sand, or stone blocks over a flat lawn so it reads as a block world.
note: The book's block is a brick and a jumper (4 plates); this adds a grass plate between to make the 5-plate cube.

name: stepped_block_terrain
title: a hill or dune that rises in square terraces on the 2-stud grid, never in slopes, its top in square patches of two or three materials.
why: Hills, dunes, and banks in a blocky scene, terraced on the block grid with patches of grass and sand.
note: VARIANT of hillside: square steps on the 2-stud grid, no slopes. Folds in voxel_color_patch_ground (the top plates' material patches).

name: block_tree
title: a blocky tree, a square trunk under a cube-ish canopy of mixed greens with see-through leaf blocks and a ragged outline, built apart and placed as a submodel.
why: A tree for any blocky scene: square trunk, cube-ish canopy in mixed greens with see-through leaf blocks.
note: VARIANT of tree. The book hangs side blocks on brackets (99207); this sketch pushes edge blocks a stud out instead, which breaks the outline without brackets. The trans-green blocks are two 1 x 2 bricks (3065), since 3003 was never made in Trans Green.

name: speckled_block_wall
title: a wall whose texture is two or three shades of one material mixed at random, the way a game draws cobblestone, moss, or planks.
why: Cobblestone, mossy, or wooden walls in a blocky build, textured by mixing two or three shades at random.
note: A color pass over a running bond, like masonry_wall in mixed shades; width 2 builds it of whole blocks.

name: mossy_stone_block
title: a gray game block with green showing in a thin band around its side, like moss in the seams.
why: A stone block with moss in its seams, for ruins, wells, and cave edges in a blocky scene.
note: The book's unit is a plate, round plates, and a jumper (3 plates); this puts it on a 2 x 2 brick to make the 5-plate cube.

name: bookshelf_block
title: a 2 x 2 game block of wood whose sides show rows of colored book spines.
why: Furniture for a blocky house: a block of book spines, alone or three in a row as a shelf wall.

name: cactus_column
title: a 2 x 2 green column of game blocks with studs on every side, the studs read as spines.
why: A desert cactus in a blocky scene: a green column with studs on every side as spines.
note: Built the way the second book does it (bricks with studs on four sides, 4733). The first book's version turns a bracket 1 x 2 - 2 x 2 up (99207) on each block, but that bracket's upright fills the 1 x 2 above its base, so it can't sit under the next 2 x 2 block as the research note has it.

name: reed_stalks
title: tall lime stalks growing from a sand block in a square of water, the game's sugar-cane look.
why: Reeds or cane at a pond's edge in a blocky scene: lime stalks from a sand square in water.

name: block_water_and_falls
title: a square pool set flush in the ground and a column of see-through blocks falling into it down a stone face, water the way a block world draws it.
why: Water in a blocky scene: a flush square pool and a column of see-through blocks falling down a stone face.
note: VARIANT of pond and waterfall: square, flush, on the grid. The book's stream also uses 2 x 2 slopes; this one is 1 x 2 bricks only, true to the no-slope rule.

name: lava_inset
title: a glowing square of lava set a plate down into a stone floor of blocks, for a forge or a cave.
why: A forge floor or a cave: a glowing lava square set a plate down in a rim of stone blocks.
note: No 2 x 2 tile in Trans Orange, so the glow layer is 1 x 2 tiles.

name: crop_field
title: a tilled field of crops in rows on dark soil, a water channel down its middle and a rim of smooth blocks around it.
why: A farm in a blocky scene: rows of crops on soil, a water channel down the middle, and a rim of jumper blocks.
note: The book's channel is a 1-wide line of tiles; on the 2-stud grid with an even field it is 2 wide here. Uses jumper_rim's method for the rim. The grass stem (15279) has no connector data but seats cleanly on its round plate.

name: block_fence_post
title: thin fence posts with stub rails sticking out four ways, each centered on its block, the way a game draws a fence.
why: A fence for a blocky farm or yard: thin posts with tab rail stubs, each centered on its block.
note: VARIANT of fence (voxel posts on jumpers). The rail plates link posts in pairs, so a long run has a gap in the rail every other bay.

name: stick_torch
title: a thin wooden stick with a glowing square flame on top, the blocky-world torch.
why: Lighting in a blocky scene: a stick with a square flame, on a block's center or a ground stud.
note: VARIANT of torch_sconce, free-standing; no wall clip version.

name: plank_and_stone_wall
title: a blocky house wall, light wood planks over a speckled stone footing, with dark log posts at its ends and a plain window set in the planks.
why: The wall of a blocky house: planks over a speckled stone footing, log posts at the ends, a plain window.
note: VARIANT of masonry_wall / clapboard_siding: two materials and log corners. The log bricks' ridges run up and down (as the part is), reading as vertical planks.

name: stepped_plank_roof
title: a gable roof with no slopes, climbing in 1-stud steps of plank-faced courses to a ridge of blocks, the blocky-world roof.
why: The roof of a blocky house: a gable climbing in 1-stud steps of plank treads to a ridge of jumper blocks, no slopes.
note: VARIANT of gable_roof. Doesn't lift off as one piece; the courses are stacked on the walls.

name: flat_jumper_roof
title: a flat roof that lifts off, tiled smooth in the middle and ringed with jumper plates so its edge reads as a row of blocks, one stud each.
why: A flat roof for a blocky forge or shed that lifts off, tiled smooth with a rim of one-stud blocks.
note: VARIANT of lift_off_roof_seat; includes jumper_rim (1 x 2 jumpers in a 1-stud ring, as on the book's forge roof).

name: block_beast
title: a game animal made of boxes, a box body on four box legs with a box head and a face of flat squares, built apart and placed as a submodel.
why: Animals for a blocky farm: a box body on box legs with a box head and a face of tiles; a pig in the default colors.
note: The book's head is a printed 2 x 2 brick; here the face is plain tiles and a sideways plate on a brick with studs on one side (11211), since Emmet uses no prints.
